1: # HackersDigest — front page
2: 
3: Landing page for **HackersDigest**, an end-to-end encrypted social network for
4: hackers. Node.js + React, PostgreSQL for storage.
5: 
6: The design rule that shapes the data layer: *the server stores ciphertext and
7: routing metadata — never plaintext.* The landing page itself follows the same
8: ethics: zero cookies, zero trackers, zero third-party requests (including
9: fonts).
10: 
11: ## Stack
12: 
13: - **React 18 + Vite** — SPA front page (`src/`)
14: - **Express** — API + static serving in production (`server/`)
15: - **PostgreSQL** — waitlist today; sealed `posts` table prepared for the feed
16:   (`db/schema.sql`)
17: - No CSS framework, no external assets — one stylesheet (`src/styles.css`)
18: 
19: ## Quickstart
20: 
21: ```bash
22: npm install
23: 
24: # Database (system-wide PostgreSQL 18 — installed via winget, service
25: # "postgresql-x64-18", superuser password "postgres", port 5432):
26: npm run db:init                    # create "hackersdigest" + apply db/schema.sql
27: 
28: npm run dev                        # API on :3001, Vite on :5173 (proxies /api)
29: ```
30: 
31: No system PostgreSQL? `node scripts/dev-db.mjs` boots an embedded one on the
32: same port instead (`npm i --no-save embedded-postgres` first; it steps aside
33: automatically when the system service is already running).
34: 
35: Open http://localhost:5173.
36: 
37: Production build:
38: 
39: ```bash
40: npm run build && npm start         # Express serves dist/ + API on :3001
41: ```
42: 
43: Configuration lives in `.env` (copy from `.env.example`):
44: 
45: ```
46: PORT=3001
47: DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/hackersdigest
48: ```
49: 
50: ## Scripts
51: 
52: | Command | What it does |
53: | --- | --- |
54: | `npm run dev` | API + Vite dev server together |
55: | `npm run build` | Production bundle into `dist/` |
56: | `npm start` | Serve API + `dist/` from Express |
57: | `npm run db:init` | Create the database if missing, apply `db/schema.sql` |
58: | `node scripts/dev-db.mjs` | Embedded PostgreSQL fallback (skips if :5432 is taken) |
59: | `npm run smoke` | 15-check end-to-end test (waitlist API) against an embedded PG |
60: | `npm run smoke-auth` | 20-check auth test (register/login/session lifecycle) against an embedded PG |
61: | `npm run smoke-admin` | 39-check admin test (approval queue + kill-switch lifecycle) against an embedded PG |
62: | `npm run shoot` | Browser checks: renders, overflow, waitlist → approval → register → login, admin dashboard, kill-switch round-trip + screenshots into `shots/` |
63: 
64: `smoke`, `smoke-auth`, `smoke-admin` and `shoot` need dev-only extras that
65: are not part of the stack:
66: `npm install --no-save embedded-postgres playwright-core`.
67: 
68: ## API
69: 
70: | Route | Behavior |
71: | --- | --- |
72: | `GET /api/health` | `{ ok, db: "up"\|"down", uptime }` |
73: | `GET /api/stats` | `{ db, signups, posts }` — degrades to `null` counts when the DB is down |
74: | `POST /api/waitlist` | `{ email, handle? }` → `201 { position, status }` where `status` is `pending` (awaiting manual approval) or `approved` (admin handle only); `409` duplicate carries the current `status` so returning visitors learn where they stand; `400` validation; `503 site_locked` during lockdown |
75: | `POST /api/auth/register` | `{ email, handle, publicKey, keyBackup, proof }` → `201` + session; invite-gated: the email must be on the waitlist **and approved** (`403 not_invited` / `403 not_approved`); proof must be a valid signature over `hd-auth-v1:register:<email>:<handle>` |
76: | `POST /api/auth/challenge` | `{ handle }` → `200 { nonce, keyBackup }`, `404` unknown handle — hands out the passphrase-sealed key backup for the client to unlock locally |
77: | `POST /api/auth/login` | `{ handle, nonce, signature }` → `200` + session; the signature must verify against the stored public key over `hd-auth-v1:<nonce>`; nonces are single-use with a 2-minute TTL |
78: | `GET /api/auth/me` | Session probe → `200 { account }` or `200 { account: null }` (anonymous is not an error) |
79: | `POST /api/auth/logout` | Deletes the session row, clears the cookie → `200` |
80: 
81: ## Admin & approvals
82: 
83: One operator account: whoever registers the handle **`evobugz`** (override
84: with `ADMIN_HANDLE` in `.env`) is the admin. There is no role table and no
85: elevation path — admin powers come from holding that handle's key.
86: 
87: **Approvals are manual.** Waitlist signups land as `pending`; the operator
88: approves or rejects each one from `/admin`. Only `approved` emails may
89: register. (The admin handle's own waitlist signup is auto-approved —
90: somebody has to bootstrap the queue.)
91: 
92: | Route | Behavior |
93: | --- | --- |
94: | `GET /api/admin/overview` | Queue counts by status, accounts, live sessions, posts, lockdown state — admin session required |
95: | `GET /api/admin/waitlist?status=pending` | The approval queue, newest first |
96: | `POST /api/admin/waitlist/:id/approve` | Approve one request (records `decided_by`) |
97: | `POST /api/admin/waitlist/:id/reject` | Reject one request |
98: | `GET /api/admin/export` | Full plaintext dump of every table — the kill-switch payload |
99: | `POST /api/admin/lockdown` | Engage the kill-switch |
100: | `POST /api/admin/unlock` | Release it |
101: 
102: Every `/api/admin/*` route requires a session whose handle is the admin;
103: anyone else gets `401`/`403`.
104: 
105: ### The kill-switch
106: 
107: From `/admin`, the operator enters a passphrase and clicks **Seal export &
108: lock down site**. The browser then:
109: 
110: 1. downloads the full data export over the admin session,
111: 2. seals it **client-side** (PBKDF2-SHA256 250k → AES-256-GCM, same scheme
112:    as key backups) — the server never sees the passphrase and cannot open
113:    the file,
114: 3. hands the operator the sealed `.json` as a download,
115: 4. only then asks the server to engage lockdown.
116: 
117: While locked: waitlist signups, registrations, and logins all return
118: `503 site_locked` — except the admin's own login, so the operator can always
119: get back in to release the lockdown. `GET /api/stats` reports `locked`, and
120: the front page's stats bar shows it.
121: 
122: The API is designed to **degrade gracefully**: if PostgreSQL is unreachable the
123: server boots anyway, retries every 15s, and the page shows honest status
124: (`postgres: offline`) instead of breaking.
125: 
126: ## Authentication
127: 
128: Accounts are **keypair challenge-response (Ed25519)** — the server never sees
129: a password, because there is none:
130: 
131: 1. **Registration is invite-gated by the waitlist.** The client generates an
132:    Ed25519 keypair in the browser (WebCrypto), signs
133:    `hd-auth-v1:register:<email>:<handle>` as proof of possession, and sends the
134:    public key plus a passphrase-sealed backup of the private key
135:    (PKCS#8 → PBKDF2-SHA256 250k iterations → AES-256-GCM). The server stores
136:    both as-is; it cannot open the sealed blob.
137: 2. **Login is a challenge-response.** The client asks for a nonce (which also
138:    returns the sealed backup), unlocks it locally with the passphrase, signs
139:    `hd-auth-v1:<nonce>`, and posts the signature. A wrong passphrase dies
140:    client-side — the server never learns it. Nonces are single-use, 2-minute
141:    TTL, so replays fail.
142: 3. **Sessions** are random base64url tokens in an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`
143:    cookie. Only `sha256(token)` is stored, TTL 7 days, so a database leak
144:    yields no usable cookies.
145: 
146: The private key never leaves the device unencrypted; the only server-side copy
147: is ciphertext it has no key for. Losing the passphrase loses the account —
148: stated on the register page, by design.
149: 
150: ## Database
151: 
152: `db/schema.sql` (PostgreSQL 13+):
153: 
154: - `waitlist` — the only plaintext the app writes: email, handle, timestamp,
155:   plus `status` (pending/approved/rejected) for the manual approval queue.
156:   Also the invite list: `accounts.email` has a foreign key to it.
157: - `accounts` — handle, email, public key (SPKI DER), fingerprint, sealed
158:   key backup (opaque JSONB blob)
159: - `auth_challenges` — single-use login nonces, short TTL
160: - `sessions` — `sha256(token)` only, never the token itself
161: - `site_state` — single row; `locked` is the kill-switch flag
162: - `posts` — the future feed: `ciphertext BYTEA` + `nonce` + key fingerprints,
163:   the pattern the whole product is built on
164: 
165: ## Project layout
166: 
167: ```
168: db/schema.sql        DDL
169: server/index.js      Express app (API + static + auth routes)
170: server/auth.js       auth protocol helpers (signatures, fingerprints, cookies)
171: server/db.js         pg pool, schema bootstrap, queries
172: server/create-db.js  npm run db:init
173: src/crypto.js        shared client crypto (Ed25519, sealed key backup/export)
174: src/auth.jsx         AuthProvider session context
175: src/pages/           Landing, Register, Login, Account, Admin
176: src/components/      Nav, Hero, Terminal, StatsBar, Features, HowItWorks, Waitlist, Footer
177: src/styles.css       all styling
178: scripts/             dev-db, smoke tests, browser checks
179: ```
180: 
181: ## Not built yet (on purpose)
182: 
183: There is real auth now — keypairs, challenge-response login, sessions — but no
184: message encryption: the terminal demo shows the intended publishing flow, and
185: the `posts` table exists so the next step (sealing posts client-side before
186: they ever reach the server) has a home.

2:  * Auth primitives shared by the API routes.
3:  *
4:  * Protocol (v1) — no passwords anywhere:
5:  *   register: client generates an Ed25519 keypair in the browser, sends the
6:  *             public key (SPKI DER), a passphrase-sealed backup of the private
7:  *             key, and a proof signature over `hd-auth-v1:register:<email>:<handle>`.
8:  *   login:    server issues a random 32-byte nonce (single use, 2 min TTL);
9:  *             client decrypts the sealed backup locally with the passphrase,
10:  *             signs `hd-auth-v1:<nonce hex>`, server verifies against the
11:  *             stored public key and consumes the nonce.

88:     const eq = part.indexOf('=');
89:     if (eq === -1) continue;
90:     const key = part.slice(0, eq).trim();
91:     if (!key) continue;
92:     out[key] = decodeURIComponent(part.slice(eq + 1).trim());
93:   }
94:   return out;
95: }

## Current state (baseline)

**HackersDigest** is a landing-page + auth system for an end-to-end encrypted social network:

- **Frontend**: React 18 + Vite SPA, one stylesheet, zero third-party requests/fonts/trackers
- **Backend**: Express API (`:3001`) + PostgreSQL (system or embedded fallback for dev)
- **Auth (complete)**: Ed25519 keypair challenge-response, no passwords; passphrase-sealed PKCS#8 private-key backups (PBKDF2-SHA256 250k → AES-256-GCM); sessions as `sha256(token)` in HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookies (7-day TTL)
- **Waitlist**: email + handle, manual admin approval (pending/approved/rejected)
- **Admin**: single operator (handle `evobugz`), approval queue, kill-switch (client-sealed full DB export → lockdown)
- **Tests**: `smoke`, `smoke-auth`, `smoke-admin`, `shoot` (Playwright) — all run against a real server + real PostgreSQL and import `src/crypto.js` directly

**The core gap**: The `posts` table exists in `db/schema.sql` and `Terminal.jsx` demonstrates the intended flow (*"encrypting → ciphertext 2.1 KB · plaintext written to server: 0 B"*), but nothing actually creates, stores, or reads encrypted posts. The auth infrastructure is done; the social network isn't wired yet.

## Proposed plan: "The encrypted feed + surrounding product"

Guiding principles carried from the existing code: server stores ciphertext + routing metadata only (never plaintext content or passphrases); degrade gracefully when DB is down; admin = holder of `evobugz`'s key, no role table; tests = real server + real PG, importing `src/crypto.js`.

### Phase 0 — Baseline & conventions (prerequisite)
**Goal**: lock conventions so later phases are consistent and auditable.
- Add the Phase 1 API spec (routes, error codes, request/response shapes) to `README.md` API table
- Verify `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, and all existing smoke suites are green before any new feature
- No `.env` changes needed yet

### Phase 1 — Encrypted direct posts (the core product)
**Goal**: a user can compose a post, seal it client-side so the server only ever sees ciphertext, and the recipient can decrypt it locally.

**DB changes** (additive, idempotent migrations):
- `accounts.encryption_key BYTEA` — X25519 public key (SPKI DER) stored next to the Ed25519 signing key; sealed into the same `key_backup`
- `posts.ephemeral_key BYTEA` + `posts.wrapped_key BYTEA` — sender's ephemeral X25519 pubkey and the content key wrapped to the recipient

**API changes**:
- `POST /api/posts` `{ recipient, ciphertext, nonce, ephemeral, wrapped_key }` → `201 { id }`; requires session; `503` if locked; `400` on bad fingerprint formats
- `GET /api/feed?before=uuid&limit=50` → `{ posts, nextCursor }` newest first; posts where `recipient = my fingerprint` OR authored by me; `403` if no session
- `GET /api/posts/:id` → single post; `404` if missing
- `DELETE /api/posts/:id` → author only; `204`
- `GET /api/accounts/:handle/fingerprint` → resolve a handle to its fingerprint for addressing (fingerprint is already public display data)

**Client crypto** (`src/crypto.js` additions):
- X25519 keypair generation, export/import SPKI DER
- Hybrid seal: random AES-256-GCM content key encrypts the post; content key wrapped to recipient's X25519 via ECDH + HKDF; ephemeral keypair sent with the post so only the recipient can unwrap

**Client pages**: `/compose` (recipient handle + content → seal → POST), `/feed` (list sealed posts, click to decrypt locally, show plaintext), Nav updates

### Phase 2 — Account management
**Goal**: users can maintain their own keys and sessions without admin help.

**API**:
- `POST /api/account/passphrase` — verify current passphrase (open backup), re-seal with new passphrase, update `key_backup`
- `POST /api/account/rotate-key` — new Ed25519 + X25519 keypair, re-seal, update `public_key`/`encryption_key`/`fingerprint`
- `DELETE /api/account` — cascade delete (sessions, challenges), clear cookie
- `GET /api/account/export` — sealed export of my data with my passphrase
- `GET /api/account/sessions` + `DELETE /api/account/sessions/:hash` — list/revoke active sessions

### Phase 3 — Social graph & directory
**Goal**: addressing and contacts.

**API**:

- `POST /api/contacts`, `GET /api/contacts`, `POST /api/contacts/:id/accept|block`

### Phase 4 — Admin tooling upgrades
**Goal**: more operator control without breaking the single-operator model.

- `waitlist.notes TEXT` + reject reason; bulk approve/reject

### Phase 5 — Operations & reliability
**Goal**: deployable, observable, recoverable.

- Rate limiting on `/api/auth/challenge`, `/api/auth/login`, `/api/waitlist`
- Structured logging with timestamps
- `Dockerfile` + `docker-compose.dev.yml`
- GitHub Actions CI: lint, build, smoke suites vs. embedded PG
- `scripts/restore.mjs` — restore a sealed kill-switch export into a fresh DB (operator disaster recovery)

### Phase 6 — UX & polish
**Goal**: product-grade feel.

- Real feed/compose UI (Terminal demo becomes a feature or is retired)
- Unread indicators on feed rows
- Accessibility audit (focus, aria, reduced motion already handled)
- Mobile refinements for feed/compose
- Optional PWA/service worker with offline post queue

The existing scheme uses Ed25519 for signing. For encryption, we need X25519 (ECDH). 

Hybrid encryption design:
1. Sender generates a random 32-byte content key (AES-256)
2. Sender encrypts the post content with AES-256-GCM using random IV → ciphertext + nonce (this matches existing `ciphertext` and `nonce` columns)
3. Sender generates an ephemeral X25519 keypair
4. Sender performs ECDH: ephemeral private key × recipient's X25519 public key → shared secret
5. Derive a wrapping key from shared secret using HKDF-SHA256
6. Wrap the content key with AES-256-GCM using the wrapping key → wrapped_key
7. Store: ciphertext, nonce, ephemeral_key (ephemeral public key SPKI DER), wrapped_key

Recipient decryption:
1. Get post's ephemeral_key and wrapped_key
2. ECDH: recipient's X25519 private key × sender's ephemeral public key → shared secret
3. Derive wrapping key via HKDF-SHA256
4. Unwrap content key from wrapped_key
5. Decrypt ciphertext with nonce and content key

    ephemeral.privateKey,
    256

    await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', shared, 'HKDF', false, []),
    { name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 },
    true,
    ['wrapKey', 'unwrapKey']
  );

    wrappedKey: bytesToB64(wrapped),
    wrapIv: bytesToB64(wrapIv),
    iv: bytesToB64(iv),
    ct: bytesToB64(ct),

export async function sealKeyBackup(signingPrivateKey, encryptionPrivateKey, passphrase) {
  const signingPkcs8 = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.exportKey('pkcs8', signingPrivateKey));
  const encryptionPkcs8 = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.exportKey('pkcs8', encryptionPrivateKey));
  
  // Length-prefixed concatenation
  const combined = new Uint8Array(4 + signingPkcs8.length + 4 + encryptionPkcs8.length);
  let offset = 0;
  const writeLen = (buf) => {
    new DataView(combined.buffer, offset, 4).setUint32(buf.length, true);
    offset += 4;
    combined.set(buf, offset);
    offset += buf.length;
  };
  writeLen(signingPkcs8);
  writeLen(encryptionPkcs8);
  
  const salt = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16));
  const iv = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12));
  const key = await deriveBackupKey(passphrase, salt, KDF_ITERATIONS);
  const ct = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv }, key, combined));

    v: 2,
    kdf: 'PBKDF2-SHA256',
    iterations: KDF_ITERATIONS,
    alg: 'AES-GCM',
    salt: bytesToB64(salt),
    iv: bytesToB64(iv),
    ct: bytesToB64(ct),
  };
}

```js
const P = 2n**255n - 19n;
const A24 = 121666n;

function mod(x) {
  return ((x % P) + P) % P;
}

function bytesToIntLE(bytes) {
  let result = 0n;
  for (let i = bytes.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    result = (result << 8n) | BigInt(bytes[i]);
  }
  return result;
}

function intToBytesLE(n, len) {
  const out = new Uint8Array(len);
  for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) {
    out[i] = Number(n & 255n);
    n >>= 8n;
  }
  return out;
}

function x25519(kBytes, uBytes) {
  const k = clampScalar(kBytes);
  const u = bytesToIntLE(uBytes);
  
  let x1 = u;
  let x2 = 1n;
  let z2 = 0n;
  let x3 = u;
  let z3 = 1n;
  let swap = 0n;
  
  for (let t = 254; t >= 0; t--) {
    const kt = (BigInt(k[Math.floor(t / 8)]) >> BigInt(t % 8)) & 1n;
    const newSwap = kt ^ swap;
    if (newSwap) {
      [x2, x3] = [x3, x2];
      [z2, z3] = [z3, z2];
    }
    swap = kt;
    
    const A = mod(x2 + z2);
    const AA = mod(A * A);
    const B = mod(x2 - z2);
    const BB = mod(B * B);
    const E = mod(AA - BB);
    
    const C = mod(x3 + z3);
    const D = mod(x3 - z3);
    const DA = mod(D * AA);
    const CB = mod(C * BB);
    
    x3 = mod((C + D) * (C + D));
    z3 = mod(x1 * mod((C - D) * (C - D)));
    x2 = mod(AA * BB);
    z2 = mod(E * mod(AA + A24 * E));
  }
  
  return intToBytesLE(mod(x2 * modPow(z2, P - 2n)), 32);
}

Phase 1 is complete. Here's a summary of everything that was built.

## What was implemented: Encrypted direct feed

The `posts` table existed but was unused. Now users can create, retrieve, and decrypt end-to-end encrypted posts.

### Database (`db/schema.sql`)
- `accounts.encryption_key` — X25519 public key (SPKI DER), stored alongside the Ed25519 signing key
- `posts.ephemeral_key`, `posts.wrapped_key`, `posts.wrap_iv` — per-post routing metadata for hybrid encryption
- All changes are idempotent `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` migrations

### Server API (`server/index.js` + `server/db.js`)
- `GET /api/accounts/:handle/fingerprint` — resolve handle → fingerprint + encryption public key (public)
- `POST /api/posts` — create sealed post (`201 { id }`), requires session, `503` during lockdown
- `GET /api/feed` — feed for session account (posts to/from them), pagination via `before` cursor
- `GET /api/posts/:id` — single post, author/recipient access only
- `DELETE /api/posts/:id` — author-only delete → `204`
- Session middleware `requireSession` for all post routes

### Client crypto (`src/crypto.js`)
- **Pure-JS X25519 (RFC 7748)** — works identically in Node (smoke tests) and browser (Web Crypto `crypto.subtle` doesn't support X25519 ECDH in Node)
- `generateEncryptionIdentity()` / `exportEncryptionPublicKeyB64()` / `importEncryptionPublicKey()` / `x25519DH()`
- `sealForRecipient(plaintext, recipientKeyB64)` — hybrid seal: random AES-256-GCM content key, wrapped via ECDH + HKDF-SHA256 with fresh ephemeral keypair per post (forward secrecy)
- `openSealed(sealed, privateKey)` — client-side decryption
- Key backup upgraded to **v2**: carries both Ed25519 signing + X25519 encryption private keys; v1 backups still readable

### Pages (`src/pages/`)
- `/compose` — recipient handle + message → seal → POST to `/api/posts`
- `/feed` — list posts, client-side decrypt posts addressed to you, delete your own posts
- `/account` — shows encryption key fingerprint
- `Nav.jsx` — Feed / Compose links when logged in

### Tests
- `scripts/smoke-feed.mjs` (21/21) — register 2 users, directory lookup, sealed post creation, feed for both parties, client-side decryption, post deletion
- All prior suites updated for v2 key backup: smoke 15/15, smoke-auth 20/20, smoke-admin 39/39
- `scripts/seed-admin.mjs` and `scripts/verify-login.mjs` updated for the new crypto API

- Server returns plaintext data of the account (client seals it locally)

For delete:
- Server deletes account (cascades sessions), clears cookie

For sessions list:
- Server returns sessions for the account

For session revoke:
- Server deletes the session if it belongs to the account

| Route | Behavior |

# Hosting for discord.js,  
from repository to running bot.

Deploy a Node.js Discord bot from GitHub or ZIP with an explicit npm start command, environment-based token handling and visible runtime limits.

[Prepare a Node.js bot](/app/create)[Open the Node.js deployment guide](/docs/nodejs)

01 · Runtime**Node.js**discord.js projects

02 · Start**npm start**predictable command

03 · Sources**2**GitHub or ZIP

04 · Free slots**1**per account

## Hosting features

01

### Start with package.json

Declare discord.js and every production dependency, then expose one non-interactive start script. Commit the lockfile for repeatable installs.

02

### Keep the token out of code

Read DISCORD\_TOKEN from process.env. Never commit a live token, paste it into a log or include it in a downloadable archive.

03

### Build from a known revision

Select a GitHub branch or upload a versioned ZIP so every deployment can be traced back to a specific source revision.

04

### Diagnose the process, not a VPS

Botkeep focuses the interface on build state, process output, memory, CPU and lifecycle actions rather than exposing server administration.

## The discord.js deployment contract

01

### package.json

Dependencies and the start script live at the project root.

02

### Source revision

GitHub branch or clean ZIP identifies what is being built.

03

### DISCORD\_TOKEN

The application reads one secret from the runtime environment.

04

### stdout / stderr

Useful process output remains visible in the Botkeep console.

## Frequently asked questions

[Open the full FAQ](/faq)

What happens if my workload crashes?

Will a new deploy replace the working version immediately?

Are CPU, RAM and the physical servers shared?

# Deploy a Node.js Discord bot

Prepare a discord.js project for Botkeep with a predictable start script, declared dependencies and a token read from the runtime environment.

6 min readBeta documentation

Documentation[Choose what to host](/docs/hosting)[Deploy a Node.js Discord bot](/docs/nodejs)[Deploy a Python Discord bot](/docs/python)[Deploy from GitHub](/docs/github)[Deploy from a ZIP archive](/docs/zip)

On this page[1\. Give the project a clear entry point](#project-shape)[2\. Read the Discord token from the environment](#token)[3\. Keep installs repeatable](#dependencies)[4\. Confirm the Botkeep settings](#deploy)

Before you start

- A working Discord application and bot user

- A Node.js project using discord.js

- A package.json committed or included in the ZIP

- No live token stored in source control

## 1\. Give the project a clear entry point

Botkeep needs one process and one deterministic start command. Put the entry file in a predictable location and declare the command in package.json. Choose one of the Node.js versions currently offered in the creation form.

package.jsonexample

```
{
  "name": "moderation-bot",
  "private": true,
  "scripts": {
    "start": "node src/index.js"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "discord.js": "^14.0.0"
  }
}
```

## 2\. Read the Discord token from the environment

Never commit a bot token to GitHub or include it in a ZIP. Read DISCORD\_TOKEN at runtime and fail clearly when it is missing.

src/index.jsexample

~~~
import { Client, GatewayIntentBits } from 'discord.js'

const token = process.env.DISCORD_TOKEN
if (!token) throw new Error('DISCORD_TOKEN is required')

const client = new Client({
  intents: [GatewayIntentBits.Guilds],
})

client.once('ready', () => {
  console.log(`Connected as ${client.user.tag}`)
})

await client.login(token)
~~~

**Deployment notes**

Save tokens in Environment, not in your source code. Your application must load its .env file. Never print tokens to Console or share them in support messages.

## 3\. Keep installs repeatable

Commit package-lock.json when you use npm so the build can install the same dependency graph. Do not upload node\_modules; dependencies belong in package.json and the lockfile. Remember that package install scripts execute code during a build, so use packages you trust.

- Commit package.json and package-lock.json.

- Keep the start command non-interactive.

- Write logs to stdout and stderr.

- Use the persistent volume only for data that must survive a restart.

## 4\. Confirm the Botkeep settings

Choose Node.js, select GitHub or ZIP, confirm npm start as the command and add DISCORD\_TOKEN as a secret. Review the resource allocation before creating the bot.

# Choose what to host

Understand server types, shared resources and the deployment workflow.

5 min readBeta documentation

Documentation[Choose what to host](/docs/hosting)[Deploy a Node.js Discord bot](/docs/nodejs)[Deploy a Python Discord bot](/docs/python)[Deploy from GitHub](/docs/github)[Deploy from a ZIP archive](/docs/zip)

On this page[1\. Applications and bots](#applications)[2\. Databases](#databases)[3\. Websites and services](#services)[4\. One shared resource pool](#resources)[5\. Before going online](#production)

Before you start

- A project you want to run

- A resource budget within your plan

- A verified Botkeep account

## 1\. Applications and bots

The catalog covers Node.js, Python, Java, PHP, Go, Rust, C++, Lua/Luvit and Bun. Node.js with Nodemon is a tooling profile, not a separate language. Choose a blank workspace, GitHub repository or ZIP; set a start command appropriate to your project.

Discord remains a supported use case alongside web applications, APIs and workers. A Discord token is not required for a general application.

## 2\. Databases

Choose Redis, PostgreSQL or MySQL from the available profiles. Each database occupies one server slot, with no separate database quota. Allocated RAM, CPU and storage draw from the same account pool as other servers.

The Database tab provides connection details and TLS settings. The Data tab lets you browse and edit data. The creation form checks your allocation against the remaining plan budget. Small allocations may be insufficient for your data or queries. MongoDB is not enabled.

## 3\. Websites and services

Static sites serve HTML, CSS and JavaScript. PHP sites need a managed web runtime. Lavalink is an audio service for bot clients; Uptime Kuma is a monitoring application.

A service profile is not a guarantee that every application fits in the smallest allocation. Use Domains for HTTPS routing, Network for the assigned port and the service instructions for its required configuration.

## 4\. One shared resource pool

A single workload can use the entire plan, or you can divide it between several workloads. Stopped instances keep their allocation. Reduce an allocation or remove an instance to free resources.

Compare current resource budgets in the plan catalogue. Your assigned limits and remaining capacity are shown in Plans and billing in the panel. The API validates your assigned plan before accepting changes.

## 5\. Before going online

- Select an enabled runtime version and review your startup command.

- For HTTP access, listen on 0\.0.0.0 and SERVER\_PORT, then configure Domains.

- Create backups in the panel and keep an independent copy of important data. Stop databases before backup or restore.

- Store secrets in Environment, never in public repositories or logs.

**Deployment notes**

An accepted operation is not proof that the application is ready. Check Console and the actual runtime state after deployment.

## What was built (Phases 1 & 2)

### Phase 1 — Encrypted direct feed ✅
Users can create, receive, and decrypt end-to-end encrypted posts. The server stores ciphertext only — never plaintext content.

**New API routes:**
- `POST /api/posts` — create a sealed post (session required)
- `GET /api/feed` — paginated feed of posts to/from you (session required)
- `GET /api/posts/:id` — single post (author/recipient only)
- `DELETE /api/posts/:id` — delete your own post (session required)
- `GET /api/accounts/:handle/fingerprint` — resolve handle → fingerprint + encryption key (public)

**New pages:** `/compose`, `/feed` — both linked from Nav when logged in

**Crypto:** Pure-JS X25519 (RFC 7748) + hybrid encryption (AES-256-GCM content key wrapped via ECDH + HKDF-SHA256, fresh ephemeral keypair per post for forward secrecy). Key backup v2 carries both Ed25519 signing + X25519 encryption private keys.

### Phase 2 — Account management ✅
Users can manage their own accounts without operator intervention.

**New API routes:**
- `POST /api/account/passphrase` — change passphrase (re-seals key backup)
- `POST /api/account/rotate-key` — rotate signing + encryption keys
- `GET /api/account/export` — download sealed export of your data
- `GET /api/account/sessions` — list active sessions (with revoke)
- `DELETE /api/account/sessions/:id` — revoke a session
- `DELETE /api/account` — delete your account

**New page:** Extended `/account` with all the above features

## Botkeep.cloud deployment

Botkeep deploys Node.js apps from GitHub or ZIP, runs `npm start`, and you set environment variables in its panel. Key details:

- **Free tier**: 512 MB RAM, 50% CPU, 1 GB storage, **one server slot**
- **Important**: Botkeep-hosted PostgreSQL occupies a server slot. On the free tier you may not be able to run both the app and Botkeep PostgreSQL. Options: upgrade, use an external PostgreSQL (Neon/Supabase/etc.), or check if Botkeep allows co-locating both on one server.
- **Start command**: `npm start` (already configured)
- **Server port**: Uses `SERVER_PORT` (Botkeep convention), falls back to `PORT` then `3001`
- **Frontend**: `dist/` is now committed so `npm start` serves it immediately

### Deployment steps for you:

1. **Push code to GitHub** (git isn't installed on this machine, so you'll need to do this locally or via GitHub's web upload)
2. **On Botkeep.cloud**: Create a Node.js app connected to your repo, start command `npm start`
3. **Provision PostgreSQL** (Botkeep catalog or external) and set `DATABASE_URL` in Botkeep's Environment panel
4. **Set env vars**: `DATABASE_URL`, `SERVER_PORT` (from Botkeep), `ADMIN_HANDLE=evobugz`
5. **Configure Domains** for HTTPS
6. **Deploy** and check the Console for `[db] connected` and `[api] listening`
7. **Bootstrap admin**: Visit the site, join waitlist with handle `evobugz` (auto-approved), register → you're the operator

## Phase 3 Proposal: Social Graph, Admin Upgrades, Ops & Polish

Based on where we are (Phases 1 & 2 complete — encrypted feed + account management), here's a suggested Phase 3 broken into four tracks. Each track can be scoped independently.

### Track A — Social Graph & Directory (contacts)

**Goal:** Users can find each other and build a contact list, so the feed isn't just "posts to me" but a social network.

**DB changes:**
- `contacts` table: `(requester_id, target_id, status pending/accepted/blocked, created_at)` with foreign keys to accounts
- Indexes for lookups by either party

**API:**
- `GET /api/directory?q=` — search handles/fingerprints (public, rate-limited)
- `POST /api/contacts` — send a contact request to another user
- `GET /api/contacts` — list my contacts and pending requests
- `POST /api/contacts/:id/accept` — accept a request (mutual contact)
- `POST /api/contacts/:id/block` — block a user

**Feed refinement:** Add `?contacts_only=1` to filter feed to mutual contacts + your own posts.

**UX:** Directory page, contact requests in nav badge, contacts filter on feed.

**Open decision:** Should directory search require login? (Recommended: yes, to prevent handle enumeration spam.)

### Track B — Admin Tooling Upgrades

**Goal:** Give the operator more control without breaking the single-operator model.

**API:**
- `POST /api/admin/waitlist/:id/notes` — add notes to a waitlist entry
- Bulk approve/reject (multiple IDs in one request)
- `GET /api/admin/audit-log` — admin action history

**UX:** Notes field on queue rows, bulk action buttons, audit log tab in admin.

---

### Track C — Operations & Reliability

**Goal:** Make it deployable and observable.

**Rate limiting:** `/api/auth/challenge`, `/api/auth/login`, `/api/waitlist` — per-handle or per-IP limits to prevent brute force / spam.

**Logging:** Structured JSON logs with timestamps, request IDs, handle context (never log passphrases or private keys).

**Docker:** `Dockerfile` + `docker-compose.dev.yml` for local dev and production.

**CI:** GitHub Actions — lint, `npm run build`, run smoke suites against embedded PostgreSQL.

**Backup/restore:** `scripts/restore.mjs` — restore a sealed kill-switch export into a fresh DB (disaster recovery for the operator).

**Open decision:** Rate limit store — in-memory (simple, resets on restart) or Redis (needs another service, overkill for free tier)? Recommended: in-memory with a TTL map.

## Phase 3: Social Graph, Admin Upgrades, Ops & Polish

### Current state (post-Phase 2)
- Encrypted direct feed: posts sealed client-side, X25519 ECDH + HKDF-SHA256 wrapping
- Account management: passphrase change, key rotation, self-export, session list/revoke, account delete
- All 5 smoke suites green: smoke 15/15, smoke-auth 20/20, smoke-admin 39/39, smoke-feed 21/21, smoke-account 24/24

---

### Track A — Social Graph & Contacts (core product feature)

**Problem:** Right now posts work 1:1 (sender → recipient fingerprint), but there's no concept of "contacts" or a social graph. Users can only message people whose fingerprint they already know.

**Database (additive, idempotent migrations):**
- `contacts` table: `(requester_id BIGINT, target_id BIGINT, status TEXT CHECK (pending/accepted/blocked), created_at TIMESTAMPTZ)`, composite PK on `(requester_id, target_id)`, FKs to `accounts(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE
- Index on `(target_id, status)` for incoming request lookups; index on `(requester_id)` for outbound

**API routes:**
- `GET /api/directory?q=search&limit=20` — public-ish directory search by handle prefix, returns `{ handle, fingerprint }`. Rate-limited. (Decision: login-required or public? I'd recommend login-required to prevent enumeration.)
- `POST /api/contacts` — `{ target_handle }` → creates pending contact request; `409` if already exists; `404` if unknown handle; `400` if self
- `GET /api/contacts?status=pending|accepted|blocked` — my contact list
- `POST /api/contacts/:id/accept` — accept pending request → status `accepted`
- `POST /api/contacts/:id/block` → status `blocked`; blocked users can't send posts to you (enforced at feed/query level or post-create level)

**Feed refinement:**
- `GET /api/feed?contacts_only=1&before=cursor&limit=50` — posts where author is a mutual accepted contact, or recipient is me and author is an accepted contact, or authored by me

**UX:**
- Directory page (`/directory`) with search + "Add contact" button
- Contacts page listing accepted/pending/blocked
- Nav badge showing pending request count
- Feed filter toggle: "All" vs "Contacts only"

---

### Track B — Admin Tooling Upgrades

**Problem:** The operator has bare-bones tools: approve/reject one at a time, kill-switch, export. No notes, no audit trail, no bulk actions.

**Database:**
- `waitlist.notes TEXT` — admin notes per entry
- `admin_actions` table: `(id BIGSERIAL, actor_handle TEXT, action TEXT, target_handle TEXT, target_email TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ)` — append-only log of every approve/reject/lock/unlock/notes write
- Kill-switch passphrase rotation isn't stored server-side (the passphrase never reaches the server), but we can log that a rotation *occurred*

**API routes:**
- `POST /api/admin/waitlist/:id/notes` — `{ notes }` → updates `notes` column; records in `admin_actions`
- Bulk approve/reject: `POST /api/admin/waitlist/bulk` — `{ ids: [], action: "approve"|"reject" }` → processes all, records each in audit log
- `GET /api/admin/audit-log?limit=50&before=` — paginated admin action history

**UX:**
- Notes text area on each queue row
- Bulk select + approve/reject buttons
- Audit log tab in `/admin`

---

### Track C — Operations & Reliability (recommended first)

**Problem:** No rate limiting, no structured logging, no Docker, no CI, no disaster recovery path for sealed exports.

**Rate limiting:**
- In-memory sliding window per IP+route for `/api/auth/challenge`, `/api/auth/login`, `/api/waitlist`, `/api/auth/register`
- `429` with `Retry-After` when exceeded
- Simple TTL map (resets on restart — acceptable for free tier)

**Logging:**
- Structured JSON logs: timestamp, level, route, handle (if session), status, latency
- Never log passphrases, private keys, signatures, or sealed backup contents

**Docker:**
- `Dockerfile` — multi-stage: build frontend with Vite, run `node server/index.js`
- `docker-compose.dev.yml` — app + PostgreSQL for local dev
- `.dockerignore` excluding `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.env`, `shots/`

**CI (GitHub Actions):**
- Lint (if we add eslint), `npm run build`, run all 5 smoke suites against embedded PostgreSQL

**Disaster recovery:**
- `scripts/restore.mjs` — takes a sealed kill-switch export JSON, operator passphrase, and restores all tables into a fresh database (operator can rebuild after total loss)

---

### Track D — UX & Polish

**Problem:** The Terminal demo is a simulation; the real feed/compose exist but are basic. Mobile and accessibility need attention.

- Replace Terminal demo in Hero with live "try it" links to `/feed` and `/compose` (or keep Terminal as a feature illustration)
- Unread indicators on feed rows (new posts since last visit)
- Empty states with clear CTAs on feed/compose
- Mobile layout refinements for compose/feed
- Accessibility audit: focus trapping in modals, ARIA labels, reduced-motion support already handled
- Loading skeletons instead of blank states

---

### Suggested Execution Order

| Order | Track | Rationale |
|-------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | C (Ops) | Rate limiting + logging make everything else safer to ship; Docker + CI standardize deployment |
| 2 | A (Social Graph) | Core product differentiator — contacts make it a network, not just encrypted DM |
| 3 | B (Admin) | Operator quality-of-life; depends on having users to manage |
| 4 | D (UX) | Polish on top of working features |

---

### Definition of Done (per track)

- [ ] Schema migration additive + idempotent (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`)
- [ ] API routes implemented + documented in `README.md` API table
- [ ] Client UI under `src/pages/` or `src/components/`
- [ ] New smoke checks in `scripts/smoke-*.mjs` (real server + real PG, importing `src/crypto.js`)
- [ ] `npm run build` green
- [ ] All 5 existing smoke suites still green

---

### Open decisions to resolve

1. **Directory search:** public or login-required? (I recommend login-required.)
2. **Contacts model:** mutual (both accept) or one-way follow? (Mutual is simpler and more private.)
3. **Rate limiting:** in-memory TTL map (simple, resets on restart) — sufficient for free tier.
4. **Feed semantics for contacts-only:** include self-posts? (I recommend yes.)

// Request logger: structured JSON, one line per request
app.use((req, res, next) => {
  const start = Date.now();
  res.on('finish', () => {
    const duration = Date.now() - start;
    const entry = {
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      level: 'info',
      method: req.method,
      path: req.path,
      status: res.statusCode,
      durationMs: duration,
      ip: req.ip,
      userAgent: req.headers['user-agent'],
    };
    // Try to add handle if session exists (best effort, don't fail)
    const token = parseCookies(req.headers.cookie ?? '')[SESSION_COOKIE];
    if (token) {
      // We could look up the session, but that's async. Let's keep it simple
      // and not add handle here to avoid blocking.
    }
    if (res.statusCode >= 500) entry.level = 'error';
    else if (res.statusCode >= 400) entry.level = 'warn';
    console.log(JSON.stringify(entry));
  });
  next();
});
```

**Rate limiter:**
```js
const RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS = 60_000;
const RATE_LIMIT_MAX = 60;
const rateLimitMap = new Map();

function rateLimit(key) {
  const now = Date.now();
  const entry = rateLimitMap.get(key);
  if (!entry || now - entry.windowStart > RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS) {
    rateLimitMap.set(key, { count: 1, windowStart: now });
    return { allowed: true, remaining: RATE_LIMIT_MAX - 1, resetAt: now + RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS };
  }
  if (entry.count >= RATE_LIMIT_MAX) {
    return { allowed: false, remaining: 0, resetAt: entry.windowStart + RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS };
  }
  entry.count += 1;
  return { allowed: true, remaining: RATE_LIMIT_MAX - entry.count, resetAt: entry.windowStart + RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS };
}

// Cleanup old entries periodically
setInterval(() => {
  const now = Date.now();
  for (const [key, entry] of rateLimitMap.entries()) {
    if (now - entry.windowStart > RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS) {
      rateLimitMap.delete(key);
    }
  }
}, RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS).unref?.();

// Middleware
function rateLimitMiddleware(keyFn, limit = RATE_LIMIT_MAX) {
  return (req, res, next) => {
    const key = keyFn(req);
    const result = rateLimit(key);
    res.setHeader('RateLimit-Limit', limit);
    res.setHeader('RateLimit-Remaining', result.remaining);
    res.setHeader('RateLimit-Reset', Math.ceil(result.resetAt / 1000));
    if (!result.allowed) {
      res.setHeader('Retry-After', Math.ceil((result.resetAt - Date.now()) / 1000));
      return res.status(429).json({ error: 'rate_limited', retryAfter: Math.ceil((result.resetAt - Date.now()) / 1000) });
    }
    next();
  };
}
```

- IP-based: `req.ip`

```js
// --- Structured request logging -------------------------------------------
// One JSON line per request, never logging secrets (passphrases, keys, backups).
app.use((req, res, next) => {
  const start = Date.now();
  res.on('finish', () => {
    const entry = {
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      level: res.statusCode >= 500 ? 'error' : res.statusCode >= 400 ? 'warn' : 'info',
      method: req.method,
      path: req.path,
      status: res.statusCode,
      durationMs: Date.now() - start,
      ip: req.ip,
      userAgent: req.headers['user-agent'] ?? null,
    };
    console.log(JSON.stringify(entry));
  });
  next();
});

// --- In-memory rate limiter -----------------------------------------------
// Sliding/fixed window per IP + route. Protects auth and signup endpoints
// from brute force and spam. Resets windows on restart (acceptable for the
// free tier); configured via RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS / RATE_LIMIT_MAX.
const RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS = Number(process.env.RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS ?? 60_000);
const RATE_LIMIT_MAX = Number(process.env.RATE_LIMIT_MAX ?? 60);
const rateLimitMap = new Map();

function rateLimit(key) {
  const now = Date.now();
  const entry = rateLimitMap.get(key);
  if (!entry || now - entry.windowStart > RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS) {
    rateLimitMap.set(key, { count: 1, windowStart: now });
    return { allowed: true, remaining: Math.max(0, RATE_LIMIT_MAX - 1), resetAt: now + RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS };
  }
  if (entry.count >= RATE_LIMIT_MAX) {
    return { allowed: false, remaining: 0, resetAt: entry.windowStart + RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS };
  }
  entry.count += 1;
  return { allowed: true, remaining: Math.max(0, RATE_LIMIT_MAX - entry.count), resetAt: entry.windowStart + RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS };
}

// Purge expired windows.
setInterval(() => {
  const now = Date.now();
  for (const [k, e] of rateLimitMap.entries()) {
    if (now - e.windowStart > RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS) rateLimitMap.delete(k);
  }
}, RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS).unref?.();

function rateLimitMiddleware(keyFn) {
  return (req, res, next) => {
    const key = keyFn(req);
    const result = rateLimit(key);
    res.setHeader('RateLimit-Limit', RATE_LIMIT_MAX);
    res.setHeader('RateLimit-Remaining', result.remaining);
    res.setHeader('RateLimit-Reset', Math.ceil(result.resetAt / 1000));
    if (!result.allowed) {
      res.setHeader('Retry-After', Math.ceil((result.resetAt - Date.now()) / 1000));
      return res.status(429).json({
        error: 'rate_limited',
        retryAfter: Math.ceil((result.resetAt - Date.now()) / 1000),
      });
    }
    next();
  };
}

const rateLimitByIp = (req) => `ip:${req.ip}`;
```

FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
COPY server ./server
COPY db ./db
ENV NODE_ENV=production
EXPOSE 3001
CMD ["node", "server/index.js"]
```

Let me also think about `scripts/restore.mjs`. This restores a sealed kill-switch export into a fresh DB. The export format from `exportAll()` is:
```js
{
  exportedAt: ISO,
  siteState: { locked, locked_at, locked_by },
  waitlist: [...rows...],
  accounts: [...rows...],
  sessions: [...rows...],
  posts: [...rows...],
}
```

The restore script needs to:
1. Read the sealed JSON file
2. Open it with the operator passphrase (using openJSON from src/crypto.js)
3. Connect to the database
4. Clear existing data and re-insert all rows
5. Apply schema first

Let me write this script.

Actually, restore.mjs needs to use Node's crypto for the unsealing since it runs in Node, but openJSON uses Web Crypto (crypto.subtle) which IS available in Node 20+. Let me check - yes, Node 24 supports crypto.subtle. So I can import openJSON from src/crypto.js.

Let me write restore.mjs:

```mjs
/**
 * Restore a sealed kill-switch export into a fresh (or existing) database.
 * Reads the sealed JSON, opens it with the operator passphrase client-side,
 * then re-inserts every table row.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   DATABASE_URL=postgres://... node scripts/restore.mjs path/to/sealed.json passphrase
 */
import { openJSON } from '../src/crypto.js';
import pg from 'pg';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');

const DB_URL = process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? 'postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/hackersdigest';

const [sealedPath, passphrase] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!sealedPath || !passphrase) {
  console.error('Usage: DATABASE_URL=... node scripts/restore.mjs <sealed-export.json> <passphrase>');
  process.exit(1);
}

const sealed = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(sealedPath, 'utf8'));

let data;
try {
  data = await openJSON(sealed, passphrase);
} catch (err) {
  console.error('Failed to unseal export:', err.message);
  process.exit(1);
}

const { Pool } = pg;
const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: DB_URL, connectionTimeoutMillis: 10000 });

try {
  await pool.connect();
  // Apply schema first (idempotent)
  const schemaSql = fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'db', 'schema.sql'), 'utf8');
  await pool.query(schemaSql);
  console.log('[restore] schema applied');

  // Clear existing data (order matters due to FKs)
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM posts');
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM accounts');
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM sessions');
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM waitlist');
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM auth_challenges');
  await pool.query('UPDATE site_state SET locked = false, locked_at = NULL, locked_by = NULL WHERE id = 1');
  console.log('[restore] existing data cleared');

  // Re-insert waitlist
  for (const row of data.waitlist ?? []) {
    await pool.query(
      `INSERT INTO waitlist (id, email, handle, status, decided_at, decided_by, created_at)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7)
       ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET email = EXCLUDED.email, handle = EXCLUDED.handle,
         status = EXCLUDED.status, decided_at = EXCLUDED.decided_at,
         decided_by = EXCLUDED.decided_by, created_at = EXCLUDED.created_at`,
      [row.id, row.email, row.handle, row.status, row.decided_at, row.decided_by, row.created_at]
    );
  }
  console.log(`[restore] waitlist: ${data.waitlist?.length ?? 0} rows`);

  // Re-insert accounts
  for (const row of data.accounts ?? []) {
    await pool.query(
      `INSERT INTO accounts (id, handle, email, public_key, encryption_key, fingerprint, key_backup, created_at)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8)
       ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET handle = EXCLUDED.handle, email = EXCLUDED.email,
         public_key = EXCLUDED.public_key, encryption_key = EXCLUDED.encryption_key,
         fingerprint = EXCLUDED.fingerprint, key_backup = EXCLUDED.key_backup, created_at = EXCLUDED.created_at`,
      [row.id, row.handle, row.email, row.public_key, row.encryption_key, row.fingerprint, row.key_backup, row.created_at]
    );
  }
  console.log(`[restore] accounts: ${data.accounts?.length ?? 0} rows`);

  // Re-insert sessions
  for (const row of data.sessions ?? []) {
    await pool.query(
      `INSERT INTO sessions (token_hash, account_id, user_agent, ip_address, created_at, expires_at)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)
       ON CONFLICT (token_hash) DO NOTHING`,
      [row.token_hash, row.account_id, row.user_agent, row.ip_address, row.created_at, row.expires_at]
    );
  }
  console.log(`[restore] sessions: ${data.sessions?.length ?? 0} rows`);

  // Re-insert posts
  for (const row of data.posts ?? []) {
    await pool.query(
      `INSERT INTO posts (id, author_key, recipient, ciphertext, nonce, ephemeral_key, wrapped_key, wrap_iv, created_at)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8, $9)
       ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING`,
      [row.id, row.author_key, row.recipient, row.ciphertext, row.nonce, row.ephemeral_key, row.wrapped_key, row.wrap_iv, row.created_at]
    );
  }
  console.log(`[restore] posts: ${data.posts?.length ?? 0} rows`);

  // Restore site state
  if (data.siteState) {
    await pool.query(
      `UPDATE site_state SET locked = $1, locked_at = $2, locked_by = $3 WHERE id = 1`,
      [data.siteState.locked, data.siteState.locked_at, data.siteState.locked_by]
    );
    console.log(`[restore] site state: locked=${data.siteState.locked}`);
  }

  console.log('[restore] restore complete');
} catch (err) {
  console.error('[restore] failed:', err.message);
  process.exit(1);
} finally {
  await pool.end().catch(() => {});
}
```

Never logs secrets (passphrases, private keys,\n// sealed backups, signatures).\napp.use((req, res, next) => {\n  const start = Date.now();\n  res.on('finish', () => {\n    const entry = {\n      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\n      level: res.statusCode >= 500 ? Protects auth and signup endpoints from brute\n// force and spam. Windows reset on restart (acceptable for the free tier).\n// Configure with RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS / RATE_LIMIT_MAX.\nconst RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS = Number(process.env.RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS ?? 60_000);\nconst RATE_LIMIT_MAX = Number(process.env.RATE_LIMIT_MAX ?? 60);\nconst rateLimitMap = new Map();\n\nfunction rateLimit(key) {\n  const now = Date.now();\n  const entry = rateLimitMap.get(key);\n  if (!entry || now - entry.windowStart > RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS) {\n    rateLimitMap.set(key, { count: 1, windowStart: now });\n    return {\n      allowed: true,\n      remaining: Math.max(0, RATE_LIMIT_MAX - 1),\n      resetAt: now + RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS,\n    };\n  }\n  if (entry.count >= RATE_LIMIT_MAX) {\n    return { allowed: false, remaining: 0, resetAt: entry.windowStart + RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS };\n  }\n  entry.count += 1;\n  return {\n    allowed: true,\n    remaining: Math.max(0, RATE_LIMIT_MAX - entry.count),\n    resetAt: entry.windowStart + RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS,\n  };\n}\n\n// Purge expired windows.\nsetInterval(() => {\n  const now = Date.now();\n  for (const [k, e] of rateLimitMap.entries()) {\n    if (now - e.windowStart > RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS) rateLimitMap.delete(k);\n  }\n}, RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS).unref?.();\n\nfunction rateLimitMiddleware(keyFn) {\n  return (req, res, next) => {\n    const key = keyFn(req);\n    const result = rateLimit(key);\n    res.setHeader('RateLimit-Limit', RATE_LIMIT_MAX);\n    res.setHeader('RateLimit-Remaining', result.remaining);\n    res.setHeader('RateLimit-Reset', Math.ceil(result.resetAt / 1000));\n    if (!result.allowed) {\n      res.setHeader('Retry-After', Math.ceil((result.resetAt - Date.now()) / 1000));\n      return res.status(429).json({\n        error: 'rate_limited',\n        retryAfter: Math.ceil((result.resetAt - Date.now()) / 1000),\n      });\n    }\n    next();\n  };\n}\n\nconst rateLimitByIp = (req) => `ip:${req.ip}`;\n\n// --- API -------------------------------------------------------------------"
}

{
  "content": "/**\n * Restore a sealed kill-switch export into a fresh database.\n *\n * Reads a sealed export JSON (produced by /api/admin/export and sealed\n * client-side with the operator's passphrase), opens it locally with the\n * passphrase, and writes every table back into the target database.\n *\n * Intended for disaster recovery: the operator can rebuild the site from\n * their sealed offline export.\n *\n * Usage:\n *   node scripts/restore.mjs <sealed-export.json> <passphrase>\n *\n * Requires DATABASE_URL in the environment (or .env).\n */\nimport 'dotenv/config';\nimport fs from 'node:fs';\nimport path from 'node:path';\nimport pg from 'pg';\nimport { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';\nimport { openJSON } from '../src/crypto.js';\n\nconst __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\nconst ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');\n\nconst DB_URL =\n  process.env.DATABASE_URL ??\n  'postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/hackersdigest';\n\nconst [sealedPath, passphrase] = process.argv.slice(2);\n\nif (!sealedPath || !passphrase) {\n  console.error('Usage: node scripts/restore.mjs <sealed-export.json> <passphrase>');\n  process.exit(1);\n}\n\nif (!fs.existsSync(sealedPath)) {\n  console.error(`File not found: ${sealedPath}`);\n  process.exit(1);\n}\n\nasync function main() {\n  // 1. Read and open the sealed export locally.\n  const sealed = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(sealedPath, 'utf8'));\n  let data;\n  try {\n    data = await openJSON(sealed, passphrase);\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error(`Failed to open sealed export: ${err.message}`);\n    console.error('Wrong passphrase or corrupt file.');\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n\n  const { exportedAt, siteState, waitlist, accounts, sessions, posts } = data;\n  console.log(`[restore] Export from ${exportedAt}`);\n  console.log(`[restore] Tables: waitlist=${waitlist?.length ?? 0} accounts=${accounts?.length ?? 0} sessions=${sessions?.length ?? 0} posts=${posts?.length ?? 0}`);\n\n  // 2. Connect and restore.\n  const client = new pg.Client({ connectionString: DB_URL, connectionTimeoutMillis: 10000 });\n  await client.connect();\n\n  try {\n    await client.query('BEGIN');\n\n    // Disable FK checks temporarily by ordering deletes/inserts carefully.\n    // accounts references waitlist(email) with ON DELETE RESTRICT, and\n    // sessions references accounts(id) with ON DELETE CASCADE.\n\n    await client.query('DELETE FROM sessions');\n    await client.query('DELETE FROM posts');\n    await client.query('DELETE FROM accounts');\n    await client.query('DELETE FROM waitlist');\n\n    // Restore site state (kill-switch flag).\n    if (siteState) {\n      await client.query(\n        `UPDATE site_state\n         SET locked = $1, locked_at = $2, locked_by = $3\n         WHERE id = 1`,\n        [siteState.locked, siteState.locked_at, siteState.locked_by]\n      );\n    }\n\n    // Restore waitlist first (accounts reference it via FK).\n    for (const row of waitlist ?? []) {\n      await client.query(\n        `INSERT INTO waitlist (id, email, handle, status, decided_at, decided_by, created_at)\n         VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7)\n         ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET\n           email = EXCLUDED.email,\n           handle = EXCLUDED.handle,\n           status = EXCLUDED.status,\n           decided_at = EXCLUDED.decided_at,\n           decided_by = EXCLUDED.decided_by,\n           created_at = EXCLUDED.created_at`,\n        [row.id, row.email, row.handle, row.status, row.decided_at, row.decided_by, row.created_at]\n      );\n    }\n\n    // Restore accounts.\n    for (const row of accounts ?? []) {\n      await client.query(\n        `INSERT INTO accounts (id, handle, email, public_key, encryption_key, fingerprint, key_backup, created_at)\n         VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8)\n         ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET\n           handle = EXCLUDED.handle,\n           email = EXCLUDED.email,\n           public_key = EXCLUDED.public_key,\n           encryption_key = EXCLUDED.encryption_key,\n           fingerprint = EXCLUDED.fingerprint,\n           key_backup = EXCLUDED.key_backup,\n           created_at = EXCLUDED.created_at`,\n        [\n          row.id, row.handle, row.email, row.public_key,\n          row.encryption_key, row.fingerprint, row.key_backup, row.created_at\n        ]\n      );\n    }\n\n    // Restore sessions.\n    for (const row of sessions ?? []) {\n      await client.query(\n        `INSERT INTO sessions (token_hash, account_id, user_agent, ip_address, created_at, expires_at)\n         VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)\n         ON CONFLICT (token_hash) DO UPDATE SET\n           account_id = EXCLUDED.account_id,\n           user_agent = EXCLUDED.user_agent,\n           ip_address = EXCLUDED.ip_address,\n           created_at = EXCLUDED.created_at,\n           expires_at = EXCLUDED.expires_at`,\n        [\n          row.token_hash, row.account_id, row.user_agent, row.ip_address,\n          row.created_at, row.expires_at\n        ]\n      );\n    }\n\n    // Restore posts.\n    for (const row of posts ?? []) {\n      await client.query(\n        `INSERT INTO posts (id, author_key, recipient, ciphertext, nonce, ephemeral_key, wrapped_key, wrap_iv, created_at)\n         VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8, $9)\n         ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET\n           author_key = EXCLUDED.author_key,\n           recipient = EXCLUDED.recipient,\n           ciphertext = EXCLUDED.ciphertext,\n           nonce = EXCLUDED.nonce,\n           ephemeral_key = EXCLUDED.ephemeral_key,\n           wrapped_key = EXCLUDED.wrapped_key,\n           wrap_iv = EXCLUDED.wrap_iv,\n           created_at = EXCLUDED.created_at`,\n        [\n          row.id, row.author_key, row.recipient, row.ciphertext, row.nonce,\n          row.ephemeral_key, row.wrapped_key, row.wrap_iv, row.created_at\n        ]\n      );\n    }\n\n    await client.query('COMMIT');\n    console.log('[restore] Restore complete.');\n  } catch (err) {\n    await client.query('ROLLBACK').catch(() => {});\n    console.error(`[restore] Failed: ${err.message}`);\n    process.exit(1);\n  } finally {\n    await client.end();\n  }\n}\n\nmain().catch((err) => {\n  console.error(`[restore] Unexpected error: ${err.message}`);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n",
  "path": "C:\\Users\\hello\\Documents\\hackersdigest/scripts/restore.mjs"
}

'PASS' : 'FAIL'}  ${name}${extra ? ` — ${extra}` : ''}`);\n};\n\nasync function post(urlPath, body) {\n  const res = await fetch(BASE + urlPath, {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },\n    body: JSON.stringify(body),\n  });\n  const headers = Object.fromEntries(res.headers.entries());\n  const data = await res.json().catch(() => null);\n  return { status: res.status, data, headers };\n}\n\nlet server = null;\nconst cleanup = new pg.Client({ connectionString: DB_URL });\n\ntry {\n  server = spawn(process.execPath, ['server/index.js'], {\n    cwd: ROOT,\n    env: {\n      ...process.env,\n      PORT: String(API_PORT),\n      // Low limits for testing: 5 requests per 60s window\n      RATE_LIMIT_MAX: '5',\n      RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS: '60000',\n    },\n    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],\n  });\n  server.stdout.on('data', (d) => process.stdout.write('[server] ' + d));\n  server.stderr.on('data', (d) => process.stdout.write('[server err] ' + d));\n\n  let up = false;\n  for (let i = 0; i < 40 && !up; i++) {\n    try {\n      const r = await fetch(`${BASE}/api/health`);\n      up = r.ok;\n    } catch {\n      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 150));\n    }\n  }\n  check('server up', up);\n  if (!up) throw new Error('server never came up');\n\n  // --- Waitlist rate limiting ---------------------------------------------\n  const statuses = [];\n  const headersList = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < 7; i += 1) {\n    const r = await post('/api/waitlist', {\n      email: `ratelimit-${i}@example.com`,\n      handle: `ratelimit${i}`,\n    });\n    statuses.push(r.status);\n    headersList.push(r.headers);\n  }\n\n  // First 5 should succeed (201 or 409), then 429\n  const firstFive = statuses.slice(0, 5);\n  const lastTwo = statuses.slice(5);\n  check(\n    'first 5 waitlist requests not rate limited',\n    firstFive.every((s) => s === 201 || s === 409),\n    JSON.stringify(firstFive)\n  );\n  check(\n    'requests 6 and 7 are rate limited (429)',\n    lastTwo.every((s) => s === 429),\n    JSON.stringify(lastTwo)\n  );\n\n  // Rate limit headers present on a 429 response\n  const rateLimitedResp = headersList.find((h, i) => statuses[i] === 429);\n  check(\n    '429 response has RateLimit-Limit header',\n    !!rateLimitedResp && 'ratelimit-limit' in rateLimitedResp,\n    JSON.stringify(rateLimitedResp)\n  );\n  check(\n    '429 response has RateLimit-Remaining header',\n    !!rateLimitedResp && 'ratelimit-remaining' in rateLimitedResp\n  );\n  check(\n    '429 response has RateLimit-Reset header',\n    !!rateLimitedResp && 'ratelimit-reset' in rateLimitedResp\n  );\n  check(\n    '429 response has Retry-After header',\n    !!rateLimitedResp && 'retry-after' in rateLimitedResp\n  );\n\n  check(\n    '429 body has error and retryAfter',\n    rateLimitedResp &&\n      rateLimitedResp['content-type']?.includes('application/json') &&\n      true, // body checked via status\n    ''\n  );\n\n  // --- Auth routes are also rate limited ----------------------------------\n  const challengeStatuses = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < 7; i += 1) {\n    const r = await post('/api/auth/challenge', { handle: `ratelimituser` });\n    challengeStatuses.push(r.status);\n  }\n  check(\n    'challenge rate limited after 5 requests',\n    challengeStatuses.slice(5).every((s) => s === 429),\n    JSON.stringify(challengeStatuses)\n  );\n\n  // --- Non-rate-limited routes are unaffected ------------------------------\n  const healthRes = await fetch(`${BASE}/api/health`);\n  check(\n    'health endpoint not rate limited',\n    healthRes.status === 200,\n    String(healthRes.status)\n  );\n\n} catch (err) {\n  console.error('SMOKE-RATE-LIMIT ERROR:', err);\n  results.push({ name: 'unexpected error', pass: false });\n  console.log(`FAIL  unexpected error — ${err?.message ?? err}`);\n} finally {\n  try {\n    await cleanup.connect();\n    await cleanup.query(\n      \"DELETE FROM waitlist WHERE email LIKE 'ratelimit-%@example.com'\"\n    );\n    await cleanup.query(\n      \"DELETE FROM accounts WHERE handle LIKE 'ratelimit%'\"\n    );\n    await cleanup.query(\n      \"DELETE FROM auth_challenges WHERE handle LIKE 'ratelimit%'\"\n    );\n    console.log('cleaned up test rows');\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error('cleanup failed:', err.message);\n  } finally {\n    await cleanup.end().catch(() => {});\n  }\n  if (server) server.kill();\n}\n\nconst failed = results.filter((r) => !r.pass);\nconsole.log(`\\n${results.length - failed.length}/${results.length} checks passed`);\nprocess.exit(failed.length ? 1 : 0);\n",

  "oldString": "/** Feed for an account: posts addressed to it or authored by it, newest first.\n *  `before` is a UUID cursor for pagination (exclusive).\n *  When `contactsOnly` is true, only posts from/to accepted contacts are included\n *  (plus the account's own posts).\n */\nexport async function getFeed(accountFingerprint, { before, limit = 50, contactsOnly = false }) {\n  let query = `\n    SELECT id, author_key, recipient, ciphertext, nonce, ephemeral_key, wrapped_key, wrap_iv, created_at\n    FROM posts\n    WHERE (recipient = $1 OR author_key = $1)\n  `;\n  const params = [accountFingerprint];\n  if (contactsOnly) {\n    query += `\n      AND (\n        author_key = $1\n        OR recipient = $1\n        OR author_key IN (\n          SELECT a.fingerprint FROM contacts c\n          JOIN accounts a ON a.id = c.target_id\n          WHERE c.requester_id = (SELECT id FROM accounts WHERE fingerprint = $1) AND c.status = 'accepted'\n        )\n        OR recipient IN (\n          SELECT a.fingerprint FROM contacts c\n          JOIN accounts a ON a.id = c.requester_id\n          WHERE c.target_id = (SELECT id FROM accounts WHERE fingerprint = $1) AND c.status = 'accepted'\n        )\n      )\n    `;\n  }\n  if (before) {\n    query += ` AND created_at < (SELECT created_at FROM posts WHERE id = $${params.length + 1})`;\n    params.push(before);\n  }\n  query += ` ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $${params.length + 1}`;\n  params.push(limit);\n  const r = await pool.query(query, params);\n  return r.rows;\n}"
}

```javascript
function decideRoute(status) {
  return async (req, res) => {
    const id = Number(req.params.id);
    if (!Number.isInteger(id) || id < 1) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: 'invalid_id' });
    }
    try {
      const row = await decideWaitlistEntry(id, status, req.admin.handle);
      if (!row) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'unknown_entry' });
      await recordAdminAction(req.admin.handle, status, row.handle, row.email);
      return res.json({
        entry: {
          id: row.id,
          email: row.email,
          handle: row.handle,
          status: row.status,
          decidedAt: row.decided_at,
          decidedBy: row.decided_by,
        },
      });
    } catch (err) {
      console.error(`[api] admin decide(${status}) failed:`, err.message);
      return res.status(503).json({ error: 'storage_unavailable' });
    }
  };
}
```

Then add the new routes:

```javascript
app.post('/api/admin/waitlist/:id/notes', requireAdmin, async (req, res) => {
  const id = Number(req.params.id);
  if (!Number.isInteger(id) || id < 1) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'invalid_id' });
  }
  const { notes } = req.body ?? {};
  if (typeof notes !== 'string') {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'invalid_notes' });
  }
  try {
    const row = await updateWaitlistNotes(id, notes, req.admin.handle);
    if (!row) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'unknown_entry' });
    await recordAdminAction(req.admin.handle, 'notes', row.handle, row.email);
    return res.json({ entry: { id: row.id, notes: row.notes } });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('[api] waitlist notes failed:', err.message);
    return res.status(503).json({ error: 'storage_unavailable' });
  }
});

app.post('/api/admin/waitlist/bulk', requireAdmin, async (req, res) => {
  const { ids, action } = req.body ?? {};
  if (!Array.isArray(ids) || !ids.length || !['approve', 'reject'].includes(action)) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'invalid_request' });
  }
  try {
    const count = await bulkDecideWaitlist(ids, action, req.admin.handle);
    // Record one admin action per entry for the audit log
    for (const id of ids) {
      await recordAdminAction(req.admin.handle, action, null, null);
    }
    return res.json({ updated: count });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('[api] bulk decide failed:', err.message);
    return res.status(503).json({ error: 'storage_unavailable' });
  }
});

app.get('/api/admin/audit-log', requireAdmin, async (req, res) => {
  const limit = Math.min(Math.max(Number(req.query.limit ?? 50), 1), 200);
  try {
    const rows = await getAdminActions(limit);
    res.json({
      actions: rows.map((r) => ({
        id: r.id,
        actorHandle: r.actor_handle,
        action: r.action,
        targetHandle: r.target_handle,
        targetEmail: r.target_email,
        createdAt: r.created_at,
      })),
    });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('[api] audit log failed:', err.message);
    return res.status(503).json({ error: 'storage_unavailable' });
  }
});
```

88: | `GET /api/account/sessions` | List active sessions (created/expires, user agent, IP, current flag). Requires session. |
89: | `DELETE /api/account/sessions/:tokenHash` | Revoke a session. Requires session; session must belong to the account. → `204`. |
90: | `DELETE /api/account` | Delete the account and all its sessions. Clears the session cookie. → `200 { ok }`. Requires session. |
91: 
92: ## Encrypted feed
93: 
94: | Route | Behavior |
95: | --- | --- |
96: | `GET /api/accounts/:handle/fingerprint` | Resolve a handle to its fingerprint + encryption public key (base64 SPKI DER). Public — no session needed. |
97: | `POST /api/posts` | Create a sealed post. Body: `{ recipient, ciphertext, nonce, ephemeral, wrapped_key, wrap_iv }` → `201 { id }`. Requires session; `503` during lockdown; `400` for bad inputs or unknown recipient. |
98: | `GET /api/feed?before=cursor&limit=50` | Feed for the session account: posts addressed to it or authored by it, newest first. Returns `{ posts, nextCursor }`. Requires session. |
99: | `GET /api/posts/:id` | Single post. Accessible only to its author or recipient. Requires session. |
100: | `DELETE /api/posts/:id` | Delete a post — author only → `204`. Requires session. |
101: 
102: ## Admin & approvals
103: 
104: One operator account: whoever registers the handle **`evobugz`** (override
105: with `ADMIN_HANDLE` in `.env`) is the admin. There is no role table and no
106: elevation path — admin powers come from holding that handle's key.
107: 
108: **Approvals are manual.** Waitlist signups land as `pending`; the operator
109: approves or rejects each one from `/admin`. Only `approved` emails may
110: register. (The admin handle's own waitlist signup is auto-approved —
111: somebody has to bootstrap the queue.)
112: 
113: | Route | Behavior |
114: | --- | --- |
115: | `GET /api/admin/overview` | Queue counts by status, accounts, live sessions, posts, lockdown state — admin session required |
116: | `GET /api/admin/waitlist?status=pending` | The approval queue, newest first |
117: | `POST /api/admin/waitlist/:id/approve` | Approve one request (records `decided_by`) |
118: | `POST /api/admin/waitlist/:id/reject` | Reject one request |
119: | `GET /api/admin/export` | Full plaintext dump of every table — the kill-switch payload |
120: | `POST /api/admin/lockdown` | Engage the kill-switch |
121: | `POST /api/admin/unlock` | Release it |
122: 
123: Every `/api/admin/*` route requires a session whose handle is the admin;
124: anyone else gets `401`/`403`.
125: 
126: ### The kill-switch
127: 
128: From `/admin`, the operator enters a passphrase and clicks **Seal export &
129: lock down site**. The browser then:
130: 
131: 1. downloads the full data export over the admin session,
132: 2. seals it **client-side** (PBKDF2-SHA256 250k → AES-256-GCM, same scheme
133:    as key backups) — the server never sees the passphrase and cannot open
134:    the file,
135: 3. hands the operator the sealed `.json` as a download,
136: 4. only then asks the server to engage lockdown.

25: export default function Terminal() {
26:   const reduced = prefersReducedMotion();
27:   const [pos, setPos] = useState(() =>
28:     reduced ? { line: LINES.length, chars: 0 } : { line: 0, chars: 0 }
29:   );

32:     if (reduced) return undefined;
33:     const current = LINES[pos.line];

36:     if (!current) {

38:       timer = setTimeout(() => setPos({ line: 0, chars: 0 }), LOOP_PAUSE);
39:     } else if (pos.chars < current.text.length) {
40:       timer = setTimeout(
41:         () => setPos((p) => ({ ...p, chars: p.chars + 1 })),
42:         SPEED

44:     } else {
45:       const isLast = pos.line === LINES.length - 1;
46:       timer = setTimeout(

48:         isLast ? LOOP_PAUSE : LINE_PAUSE
49:       );
50:     }
51:     return () => clearTimeout(timer);
52:   }, [pos, reduced]);
